rows.what_the_ink_shows: In crops/43_scan178_H0442_target.png the label begins multiplicatif and ends with the low connected strokes of connexe. At their junction, a tall narrow stroke with a rightward angled arm resembles a k immediately after the descending terminal stroke of multiplicatif. The k-like form agrees with the initial letter of the upper k.connexes label in crops/43_scan178_H0442_top_label.png and with the k-form in crops/43_scan178_H0442_unipotent_label.png. Comparison with the other spellings of multiplicatif in crops/43_scan178_H0442_multiplicatif_comparison.png and crops/43_scan178_H0442_separable_comparison.png favors treating it as an additional k, but the joined terminal f/k area remains cramped. A separate hyphen or dot at the join is not securely visible.
rows.note: The source is explicitly “a model pass of Hua’s project”, and the evidence explicitly says “not checked by a person”; this is not a personal Michel Hua facsimile check. The k-connexe reading is favored by the visible extra k-like stroke and the local comparisons, but the original no-k reading remains possible at the resolution supplied. Replace the existing single uncertain phrase with \unsure{multiplicatif k-connexe|multiplicatif connexe}, placing the supplied proposed reading first and retaining the original alternative. The punctuation joining k to connexe is part of that uncertain proposed reading, not a claim that a separate hyphen has been identified. No other diagram labels are changed.
